literature_proposed.summary: Elementary, and provable from the pinned Mathlib without analytic number theory: take n = 6·P·m² (not a prime power), B₀ = n·m², and b_s = 1 + n·B₀!·s for s = 1..B₀. Every prime factor p of Φ_n(b_s) is ≡ 1 (mod n), hence ≡ 1 (mod P), is larger than B₀ > 2m²+m, and is at most b_s^n, so log₂ p is polynomial in m. The b_s are distinct roots of X^n − 1 in ZMod p (p > B₀ ≥ s), and X^n − 1 has at most n roots, so the B₀ = n·m² values of s meet at least m² distinct primes; the product bound 2^(1000·P³·m¹²) is crude. Mathlib pieces: Polynomial.isRoot_cyclotomic_iff / orderOf_eq_of_pow_and_pow_div_prime, Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_not_prime_pow, sub_one_pow_totient_lt_cyclotomic_eval, Polynomial.card_nthRoots, Finset.card_le_mul_card_image. About 300 lines; the partial PR #1024 above it proves everything else of Luca–Tachiya's theorem for 0/1 sequences.
